newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Rank plans to sell film distribution arm.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Rank plans to sell film distribution arm.

text.p: Rank Group Plc chief executive Andrew Teare said on Thursday that the company planned to sell its Rank Film Distributors arm.
"We've had approaches and are currently seeking a bidder," Teare told Reuters in an interview.

Rank Film Distributors has a library of classic British movies, along with foreign rights to some more modern American movies. It also has a UK distribution operation, run as a joint venture with Castle Rock-Turner, and an international sales arm.
Teare said some of the valuations placed on the unit in the press were a little high. Newspapers have speculated that Rank could raise between 100 and 150 million pounds through the sale.
Many of the movies in its catalogue are quite old and the library has been heavily pre-sold for some time to come, limiting the upside for a buyer.
Teare said that Rank had raised 230 million pounds from disposals since it said last year that it planned to sell off business worth 300 million.
Rank's 1996 results were badly hit by a 232 million exceptional charge as it took a hefty 148 million property write-off plus a loss on disposals and resturcturing costs.
"This is what was expected, we've flagged it all along," he said. He said that the business had continued to move forward while the company carries out its restructuring.
